newsitem.title: GERMANY: German farmers support European currency union.
newsitem.headline: German farmers support European currency union.

text.p: The German farm union DBV at a seminar on Monday gave its unreserved support for European currency union in 1999.

"Farmers urgently need the euro because its introduction would eliminate risks from currency swings," DBV vice president Gerd Sonnleitner said in remarks prepared for delivery at the seminar, which gathered 100 agricultural decision-makers.
German farmers had been grappling with currency disadvantages because of the strong mark for the last 30 years, Sonnleitner said.

Because farm product prices were tied to the Ecu, farmers in strong currency countries had lost income and competitiveness whenever their "green" currencies, which convert arable area and other aid into national currencies, were revalued.
Sonnleitner said an effective agrimonetary regime needed to be maintained after currency union in January 1999 because not all European countries would participate.

Manfred Schoepe, head of the department for agricultural economics and politics at the Ifo research institute in Munich, said if the euro was introduced today German and French farmers stood to lose only small sums.
But their competitors in Ireland, Sweden and Denmark would suffer sharp cuts in their compensation payments and market support prices.

The switch would be costly and complicated because those inside the new currency union and those outside needed to lay down new rules on how to manage currency diversions without distorting trade across currency borders.

One way of achieving this could be to replace a country's "green rate" outside the euro bloc with its free market currency rate versus the euro, while safeguarding the right to compensation should severe currency disadvantages develop.

Karin Gress, an analyst with Landwirtschaftliche Rentenbank, said the euro would create more price transparency and harmonise competition so that efficient marketing and low cost structures would be rewarded.
